analysis.title: Rates Spark: Don't expect a break back below 5%
key_insights: ING expects the US 10-year Treasury yield to stay above 5.00% and head back up to 5.25%. A break below 5% on the 10yr would surprise the author.

Buyers appeared in Treasuries around 5.3% after Wednesday's CPI release, and again after the Asian open when equities fell, with Korean equities the focus. Ongoing buying over recent weeks has not produced a meaningful drop in yields because it was offset by net shorts in Treasury futures.

Thursday's data (low jobless claims, firm retail sales, PPI described as uncomfortably high) did not move Treasuries much. ING expects the market to use the recent calm as a platform to rebuild higher yields over the coming weeks and into the mid-terms.
Neither political side has voiced an intention to act on the fiscal deficit. High printed inflation and a high deficit remain the issues behind the yield view.

ING sees at least one more leg of long-end weakness, which could take the US 10yr into a 5.25% to 5.5% range, with other markets moving in a similar but smaller way. It sees an overshoot toward 5.5% possible, with yields elevated for months and potentially into Q1 2027.
In the eurozone, France sets the mood. The French 10yr swap spread has doubled from about 60bp to about 120bp, and French spreads to Germany are about as wide as at any point since the euro began.

ING says the French widening is probably overdone, because a swing to the right could carry tail positives not currently priced. Italian spreads have improved gradually since Meloni took office and have been low beta to French concerns.

The first real widening in French spreads traces to Macron's mid-2024 election gamble. The recent spike extends that underlying tension, and ING says further upside overshoots in bond yields are foreseeable.
